after.basis: The 1712 Stichill James, explicitly indexed as Patrick Glasow and Helen Fairbarn’s son, is confidently inferred to be the James who married Elizabath Tait in the same parish in January 1740. An age of about 28, continuity in this small local surname family and the later household’s son Patrick (1742) and daughter Helen (1750), repeating both proposed paternal grandparents’ names, form a combined identity argument. Naming is supporting evidence rather than a mandatory rule or independent proof of each step. The specific Patrick/Helen household is independently established by their 1707 marriage entries and 1708–1716 children. Newly inspected printed court minutes place Patrick at Stichill in 1712 and appoint him a burlaw man in 1715; these add local continuity, not a father clause. The unsupported Uphall field is not a competing contemporary record. No concrete rival Stichill James family has been identified in the held material; this is not an exhaustive population search.
